case: PostgreSQL domain-over-enum array XLSX re-import through Gnumeric
contract: The native domain-over-enum array contains literal NULL, an empty label, Unicode, comma and quote labels, markup, =1+1, and SQL NULL; native type, array_to_json and array_send oracles pass before export and after SQL replay.
BookiE writes the array as a string cell without a formula.
Gnumeric ssconvert opens source.xlsx, saves gnumeric-roundtrip.ods, then saves gnumeric-roundtrip.xlsx; the exact array text is unchanged, remains a string cell, and no formula is created.
The checker pins the full escaped array literal, including the formula-shaped label and the distinction between literal NULL and SQL NULL.

native_export_test.command: rtk proxy env BOOKIEE_XLSX_REIMPORT_ARTIFACT=<evidence-dir>/source.xlsx cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration domain_array_file_export_contract::value_contract_domain_enum_array_file_exports_preserve_values_and_native_type -- --include-ignored --exact --test-threads=1

steps: Install Gnumeric in the pinned Debian container.

consumer_assertions.method: Python standard-library ZIP/XML checks exact A2 text in source and re-saved ODS/XLSX, requires string cell types and rejects formulas.
consumer_assertions.result: Full domain-over-enum array text preserved, including the escaped formula-shaped label.

remaining: Other spreadsheet applications, array shapes and the broader B3 matrix remain open.
